newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal up, carloads down from yr ago.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal up, carloads down from yr ago.

text.p: U.S. intermodal rail traffic rose sharply while carload freight fell in the week ended July 19 compared to the same week last year, Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
AAR said intermodal freight rose 8.8 percent in the week to 171,180 trailers and containers from 157,272 in the year-ago week.

U.S. rail carloads fell 1.7 percent in the week to 339,140 from 344,886 a year ago, while ton-miles also declined 0.8 percent to 25.9 biilion from 26.1 billion a year ago. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, is one ton of freight hauled one mile.

Grain loadings also fell 4.6 percent to 21,059 carloads in the week from 22,073 a year ago, while coal carloads dipped 3.8 percent to 131,178 carloads from 136,358. Other declines from the year ago were seen in pulp, paper and allied products, metals and related products, and primary forest products.

In the first 29 weeks of 1997, AAR said intermodal freight increased 7.1 percent to 4.72 million trailers and containers from 4.40 million in the same 1996 period. Ton-miles were up 1.8 percent to 760.4 billion from 746.7 billion, while carloads rose 1.4 percent to 9.80 million from 9.67 million in the period, it said.

Separately, AAR reported that U.S. carloads on the two Canada-based railroads had 50,470 carloads in the July 19 week, up 9.9 percent from the year-ago week, and 24,859 trailers and containers, up 13.5 percent from a year ago.

Combined U.S. carload volume in the United States and Canada-based railroads for the first 29 weeks of 1997 totaled 11.32 million, up 1.6 percent from the same 1996 period, and 5.42 million trailers and containers, up 7.7 percent from the year-ago period, AAR said.

Among carloads, AAR said petroleum loadings posted the largest increase compared to the year-ago week, rising 6.3 percent to 5,755 from 5,415. Coke loadings increased 4.8 percent to 5,574 carloads from 5,319 a year ago, while lumber and wood loadings were up 1.9 percent to 5,542 carloads from 5,438.
Chemicals, crushed stone, sand and gravel, and stone, clay and glass loadings were also up from the year-ago week.

The largest carload declines were in grain mill products, down 10.9 percent to 8,814 carloads in the latest week from 9,887 in the year-ago week, and in farm products other than grain, off 10.2 percent to 1,248 from 1,390.
